name: Urban Company Ltd
title: Urban Company Ltd - 544515 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Urban Company's Q2 FY27 shows NTV up 39.1% to ₹1,432.3 crore and loss-making Native and International narrowing, but the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and continued aggressive spending keep losses elevated.

guidance.quote: achieve our breakeven goal by Q3 FY28
We expect the overall growth of Q2 and Q3 put together to be in the range of 50% to 55%.

summary.headline: Urban Company's consolidated NTV rose 39.1% to ₹1,432.3 crore in Q2 FY27, with adjusted EBITDA (ex-Native/International investment) at ₹30 crore, up 213% YoY.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated NTV up 39.1% YoY to ₹1,432.3 crore and revenue from operations up 41.4% to ₹537.3 crore, with adjusted loss of ₹144 crore after a ₹174 crore investment in Native. Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments, and management reiterated breakeven for the consolidated business by Q3 FY28 and a ₹1,000 crore EBITDA-type goal for FY31. Management announced a fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore, framed as flexibility rather than a need to fund losses. Q&A focused on the rationale for the raise, Native's AC launch, professional supply, and pricing/contribution economics.

financial_highlights.change: +213% YoY; ₹119 crore for trailing four quarters, +175%
vs NTV growth of 26%, per management
up 110 bps (from prior level per call)

segments.name: Core Services (India)
segments.commentary: Management said Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments and contribution margin rose to 3.5%; NTV growth was attributed to new-customer acquisition, repeat cohorts and densification, with instant service now used in top 7–8 cities.

segments.name: International (UAE, Saudi, Singapore)
segments.commentary: International NTV grew 66.2% YoY per management, with UAE described as a key market; adjusted EBITDA margin was 2% of NTV, improved by 190 bps. Management said war-related concerns are behind it and Q2+Q3 combined growth is expected at 50–55%.

segments.name: Native (water purifiers / AC services)
segments.commentary: Native's loss narrowed by ₹220 crore (per call) with loss per order down 19% QoQ to ₹279; management says Native is being built deliberately with a ₹174 crore investment in Q2 and is in a learning phase for its first AC device.

segments.name: Insta Help (professional/household help)
segments.commentary: Management said Insta Help is in a tougher base with Q2 revenue growth at 26.3% and the festive season falling in Q3; penetration in top 8 cities for largest categories is below 10%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated breakeven target reiterated for Q3 FY28; management said it is confident, more than ever, of the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal.
Management expects Q2 plus Q3 combined international growth in the range of 50% to 55%.
Fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore is for flexibility, mainly for organic build-out of existing businesses and selective M&A; management said nothing imminent.
Native AC device launch: management expects one to two quarters of learning, limited largely to the app, and no material change to Native's trajectory.
Contribution margin target of 9–10% noted as the key lever; management said it is working towards it.
capex_capacity: Orders rose 63% QoQ to 6.23 million; 45% of new orders are reportedly from the Core Services' top categories, per management.
Management is onboarding professionals aggressively in the 3–4 months before the festive season to improve the liquidity coefficient.
Native's offline distribution is in a learning phase; M3 water purifier and Lock Ultra launched in modern retail with pull from offline ecosystem.
Gold premium service rollout: management said results are promising and it intends to scale it out across categories.
demand_pricing: Core Services average spend growth slowed to around 3% (vs historical 6–7%); management attributed this to mix change and season timing, and pass-through of densification benefits in pockets.
Instant service delivered in 30–60 minutes is offered in UAE and Singapore; management said no premium is currently charged.
Professional (partner) supply grew 16% YoY versus NTV growth of 26%; management declined to give forward partner-growth projections.
Hourly pricing roughly ₹200 and net order value roughly ₹300 for an average order of 1.5 hours; partner payout of ₹150 per utilised hour.
Management described the household-help TAM as range-bound with no single winner, and the AC TAM as roughly 10x water purifier TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Core Services' accelerating new-user acquisition and is it sustainable, with average spend growth slowing to 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a stronger product with instant service in top 7–8 cities, AI-led training/QC improving word of mouth, densification, faster growth in Tier-2 markets and higher marketing. Average spend slowed due to mix, seasonality and some densification benefit passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of proceeds from the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and the M&A framework?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly for flexibility and organic build-out; M&A would be for consolidating existing categories or entering new categories, not new countries, with buy-vs-build tilting to buy if accretive. Nothing imminent.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise capital now given cash on balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise is for flexibility, to be aggressive, pursue acquisitions and absorb downside in a high-competition scenario; not primarily to fund losses. Targets remain unchanged, and they would have changed short/medium-term targets if funding were insufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Native AC launch and its allocation impact profitability timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Native is on track for profitability, AC will be a disciplined build-up with R&D the bulk of losses, and any new category would take one to two quarters of learning before scale.

qa_highlights.question: Is professional supply or retention a rate limiter, and what is steady-state unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the challenge is retaining high-quality professionals, not sourcing. Experts care about net take-home pay; the company frames pricing and payouts as competitive. Steady-state unit economics remain under evaluation with a cited framework of payout ₹150 per hour, with ₹50 covering costs at best utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the acceleration in professional-services growth and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said professional growth of 16% is a leading indicator; drivers are utilisation, targeting, and onboarding. Management declined to give specific projections.

qa_highlights.question: Will Native offline distribution expand pan-India in modern retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline share is small and in a learning phase; modern retail response is good; management will expand calibrated and slowly.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity in Core Services and International; management says losses are a deliberate choice.
Average spend growth slowing to 3% versus historical 6–7%.
Professional partner retention and churn as supply expands.
Native profitability and AC device adoption, with a one-to-two-quarter learning phase before scale.
Use and deployment of the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and any M&A execution.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on growth, profitability trajectory and the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal, with management repeatedly calling Native's losses a deliberate choice. More guarded on specifics: declined to give partner-growth projections, did not quantify average-spend slowdown beyond mix and seasonality, and said the AC launch would be calibrated and slow.

adds.what: Native AC device launch (learning phase, mainly app-limited; not a capacity addition)

growth.why: Consolidated NTV grew 39.1% YoY to ₹1,432.3 crore and Q2+Q3 international growth is guided at 50–55%, but the company is adding no owned capacity, and the ₹174 crore Native investment is an operating loss funding item rather than capacity.
